title: Premium skincare packaging print-prep: neutralize eight mixed-light serum shots to an in-frame grey card, vectorize the wordmark, build a botanical spot panel, export the authored dieline, and data-merge one press-ready label per SKU
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief (cand_64, db_i 271: 'create premium, visually appealing packaging for our beauty and skincare product line', design front/back/side panels, develop typography/colour/hierarchy, 'prepare print-ready production files', understanding of 'dielines, bleed, CMYK, and print production'; deliverables = final concepts, editable source files, print-ready PDFs, high-res mockups) and laundered to a coined fictional brand, 'Soravell Botanics' — no real company, product, or trademark is named. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the Adobe connector CANNOT compose a layout from scratch and CANNOT bind merge fields into a convert_pdf_to_indd output, so the client is modeled as supplying the AUTHORED production files (a folding-carton dieline .ai and a single-record label .indd carrying live <<fields>> plus three @-image columns) and the connector does the legitimate, repeatable production the brief rewards: neutralize a batch of eight differently-lit serum-bottle captures to the 18% grey card each one carries so the whole set shares one white point, prep-and-vectorize the scanned wordmark, build a brand-green botanical spot panel from the leaf art, produce a seasonal masked seal-colour variant without a reshoot, EXPORT the authored dieline to a print PDF, and DATA-MERGE the eight SKU rows onto the authored label to produce one press-ready label per SKU. This STRENGTHEN removes the original spec's broken convert_pdf_to_indd merge path and its single-hero amputation; no generative fill, no from-scratch art, no by-prompt compositing.
one_line_ask: Bring Soravell Botanics' eight existing serum-bottle photos to one consistent, true-to-product look by neutralizing each to the grey card it carries (deciding per frame how far to move white balance without killing any serum's genuine colour), produce a seasonal deeper seal colourway of the hero without reshooting, get the scanned wordmark clean and razor-sharp as a vector, build a brand-green botanical spot panel, export the client's authored carton dieline to a print PDF, and data-merge the roster onto the client's authored single-record InDesign label to hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI label per SKU.
full_brief: Soravell Botanics is taking an eight-SKU facial-serum line to retail and needs retail-ready packaging production. We are NOT reshooting. We are handing you eight existing serum-bottle photos, and here is the problem: they were shot across two sessions under different light — some under cool fluorescents, some under warm window or tungsten light, a couple mis-exposed — so straight out of the folder they look like a mismatched jumble, and a shelf set of mismatched shots reads cheap. To make this checkable we laid a photographic 18% grey card into a corner of every shot. Your job on the photos: bring every image to a consistent, true-to-product look by neutralizing each one to the grey card it contains — the card must read as a clean neutral grey (equal across the channels) in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole set will share one white point. Hold a subtle premium warmth in the final look, but do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch: each photo was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure and tone decision to land on the shared target. Be careful — some of these serums are genuinely coloured (a rosehip oil that is meant to look warm golden-amber, a golden vitamin-C serum, a green-tea serum): if a bottle's grey card already reads neutral, do not 'cool' it chasing an imagined cast, or you will strip the colour we are selling. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure moves you made on each frame so we can confirm they are matched, not eyeballed. Second, a seasonal colourway without a reshoot: on the Retinol Night hero the wax-seal band on the dropper collar is currently a warm terracotta-red — give us a deeper seasonal oxblood/burgundy version of the same shot (a rich, dark wine-red in the SAME colour family, deepened and slightly muted, not a jump to a far-off hue), and the recolour must sit under the real folds, sheen and shadow of the seal. No flat dead-fill, no whole-image tint bleeding onto the glass and cap — just the seal band. Third, our wordmark only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper — get it clean and razor-sharp for the label masthead and carton so it does not look like a fuzzy scan when printed. Fourth, we need the botanical side-panel motif turned into a clean brand-green spot-style texture that prints tidy. Fifth, export our carton dieline (we built it in Illustrator with real cut/fold/bleed/registration) to a print PDF as-is. Finally, build the labels: we have hand-built the InDesign single-record label template with the real placeholder fields and three image slots (the product photo, the wordmark masthead, the botanical panel), and we are giving you the roster; merge them so every SKU gets its own single-page label with its copy bound, its matching graded photo, the crisp wordmark and the panel dropped in, then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI label PDF covering every SKU (one page per SKU). Bind the copy verbatim from the roster — do not rewrite our names, actives, volumes or batch codes. Also give us a high-res mockup of the finished carton. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set matched to one white point; the seal recolour natural under the existing light; the wordmark a crisp vector; the panel a clean brand-green spot texture; and exactly one finished label per roster row.

inputs.name: soravell_label_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD serum bottle label, 70x90mm + 3mm bleed, CMYK, ONE product per page. It carries live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<product_name>>, <<key_actives>>, <<volume>>, <<batch>> laid out to a defined typographic hierarchy (product name large serif, actives medium, volume + batch small), AND THREE @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to three separate image frames: a product-shot frame bound to @photo (the row's graded bottle crop), a masthead frame bound to @wordmark (the vectorized brand wordmark), and a side-panel frame bound to @panel (the botanical spot texture). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the wordmark and the botanical panel reach the label ONLY as merge binds through these image frames. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and all three image frames actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record label is the correct, connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, never a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would NOT bind (the original spec's convert_pdf_to_indd merge path is removed). THREE image columns (@photo per-row, @wordmark shared, @panel shared) give the chain-produced wordmark SVG and duotone panel a real connector-doable path onto every label without any free-form placement.

inputs.name: soravell_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns product_name,key_actives,volume,batch,@photo,@wordmark,@panel holding 8 serum SKU rows, one per product: 'Rosehip Renewal Facial Serum' / 'Cold-Pressed Rosehip Oil + Vitamin C' / '30 ml' / 'SR-RR-0426'; 'Niacinamide Clarity Facial Serum' / '10% Niacinamide + Zinc' / '30 ml' / 'SR-NC-0426'; 'Hyaluronic Hydra Facial Serum' / '2% Hyaluronic Acid + Provitamin B5' / '30 ml' / 'SR-HH-0426'; 'Vitamin C Bright Facial Serum' / '15% Ascorbic Acid + Ferulic' / '30 ml' / 'SR-VB-0426'; 'Squalane Calm Facial Serum' / 'Plant Squalane + Ceramides' / '30 ml' / 'SR-SC-0426'; 'Retinol Night Facial Serum' / 'Encapsulated Retinol 0.3% + Peptides' / '30 ml' / 'SR-RN-0426'; 'Green Tea Detox Facial Serum' / 'Green Tea Polyphenols + Niacinamide' / '30 ml' / 'SR-GT-0426'; 'Peptide Firm Facial Serum' / 'Signal Peptides + Marine Collagen' / '30 ml' / 'SR-PF-0426'. The @photo column names the matching prepped bottle crop the merge drops into that row's product frame (e.g. @rosehip_graded.jpg). The @wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file — @soravell_wordmark.svg — in EVERY row. The @panel column holds the SAME botanical spot texture — @botanical_panel_green.png — in EVERY row. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields and the three @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Columns state product data GOALS only — no treatment/type/order column, no lighting or correction hint, nothing that telegraphs which capture is which SKU or how any frame must be corrected. Headers match the authored .indd fields and all three @-image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy, the correct per-SKU photo, the shared wordmark, and the shared panel. @wordmark and @panel carry the identical shared file path in all eight rows; @photo names the per-SKU output the AGENT produces and names after identifying each bottle by eye. Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight finished label pages.

inputs.name: raw_bottle_captures_x8.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 8 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera captures of premium amber/frosted-glass facial-serum bottles with matte dropper caps, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera before crop), each with a photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference, each on a seamless studio sweep. Shot across two sessions under deliberately mismatched light and framing, in a NEUTRAL order that does not group by treatment: (1) a bottle of deep golden-amber rosehip serum whose oil is GENUINELY warm orange-amber, shot under near-neutral light so its grey card already reads neutral (the warmth is the real product, not a white-balance error), level; (2) a pale clear niacinamide serum under cool bluish fluorescents, frame tilted ~4 deg; (3) a clear hyaluronic serum under warm window light, level; (4) a golden vitamin-C serum under a cool cast, tilted ~3 deg (its gold is real product colour); (5) a milky squalane serum, flat and underexposed, level; (6) an amber retinol serum under warm tungsten with a coloured wax-seal band around the dropper collar, tilted ~3 deg (hero for the seasonal seal recolour); (7) a greenish green-tea serum under a cool cast, tilted ~4 deg; (8) a clear peptide serum, slightly overexposed and warm, level. Every shot has real glass refraction, specular highlights, faint dust on the sweep, candid commercial-photography realism, no CGI gloss. The 18% grey card is clearly visible and uncropped in each frame.
inputs.realism_notes: TRAP + divergent-correction set. REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4000-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each product crop can fill the ~827x1063 px label image frame at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere. Deliberately mismatched (per-frame WB, exposure and tilt vary) so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set: cool frames 2/4/7 must WARM, warm frames 3/6/8 must COOL, frame 5 needs an EXPOSURE lift, frame 8 needs an exposure PULL — opposite directions, all driven to each frame's own in-frame grey card so all eight converge on one shared white point. Capture 1 is THE TRAP: its warmth is genuine rosehip-oil product colour and its grey card is already neutral, so the naive 'warm the batch / cool an imagined cast' move pushes its card off-neutral and strips the amber the brand is selling; the correct path reads THAT card by eye and HOLDS white balance. Capture 4 is a milder near-trap (real gold, cool cast — warm to neutral WITHOUT desaturating the gold). Capture 6 carries the wax-seal band for the masked recolour. Filenames are a NEUTRAL zip-address scheme (capture_01..capture_08) so nothing discloses which bottle is which SKU or which frame is the trap — the agent must open each, identify the SKU by eye, and decide its correction. Delivered as a zip of 8 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs.

inputs.name: mark_ref_01.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat scan-style raster of the 'SORAVELL BOTANICS' wordmark inked on slightly warm off-white textured paper: an elegant high-contrast serif with a small single-line botanical sprig mark centred above the text, deep forest-green letters. Rendered as a real desktop scan — the paper is a warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and edges are a touch soft. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it vectorizes to crisp paths. ~2400 px on the long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: One of two same-kind raster marks (mark_ref_01.png / mark_ref_02.png) delivered under a NEUTRAL scheme so nothing in the filename says which needs which treatment — the agent must open both to decide. THIS one is flat, high-contrast line/letter art on paper, so the correct route is prep-before-trace (straighten -> crisp -> crop-to-bounds -> knock the off-white ground to transparency -> vectorize) into a clean wordmark SVG for the carton and label masthead. Feeding it to vectorize RAW would trace the paper ground and the skew.

inputs.name: mark_ref_02.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL close-up product photograph of a finished folding-carton sample sitting on a table, the 'SORAVELL BOTANICS' logo pressed into the card as GLOSS-FOIL EMBOSS: raised metallic-green foil catching a soft raking highlight, visible card grain, a faint drop shadow under the box edge, shallow depth of field, subtle background clutter. ~3000 px on the long edge. Photographic, textured, not flat art.
inputs.realism_notes: The SECOND same-kind mark and the deliberate TRIAGE decoy: it LOOKS like 'another logo file' but it is a PHOTOGRAPH of foil emboss on textured card, not flat art. Routing it to image_vectorize like the flat mark returns garbage weave/emboss/highlight paths (a failure invisible until the SVG is opened). The correct route is image_remove_background to lift the carton sample onto a clean ground as the high-res packshot mockup — it is NOT traced. Neutral filename so the agent cannot tell from the name that this is a photo, not art.

inputs.name: motif_source.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A single continuous-line botanical illustration of overlapping eucalyptus and rosehip leaves with small berries, fine even line weight, deep green on a white background, decorative composition suitable for a packaging side panel, ~2400x3600 px, flat with no shading or gradients.
inputs.realism_notes: Two-tone-friendly line art so a halftone + single-hue tint conversion to a brand-green spot-style side panel is realistic and prints clean. Fed via crop-to-panel-bounds -> halftone -> monochromatic green tint; the result binds into every label through the template's shared @panel image frame.

inputs.name: dieline.ai
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine Adobe Illustrator .ai (PDF-compatible) folding-carton dieline for a 40x40x120 mm serum box — front, back, two side panels, top and bottom tuck flaps, dust flaps — with cut lines and fold/score lines on separate layers, 3 mm bleed, registration marks, CMYK document, and placeholder rectangles labelled FRONT/BACK/SIDE for artwork. A real structural production file.
inputs.realism_notes: Modeled as a CLIENT-AUTHORED Illustrator file because the connector can only EXPORT a genuine .ai (document_render_vector), never compose a dieline from scratch. Carries real cut/fold/bleed/registration structure so the export is a faithful print artifact; the connector EXPORTS it, it does not author it.

outputs.name: graded_serum_photos_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized, straightened serum-bottle photos, delivered as the product-framed crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, ALONGSIDE their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE decoupled claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a hair of zero) with all eight matched to one shared white point while holding a subtle premium warmth, and true-to-product (no bottle's genuine serum colour forced off, capture 1's amber and capture 4's gold intact); (b) card-exclusion is checked SEPARATELY on each delivered product crop (the *_graded output that binds into that SKU's label) — framed on the bottle with the grey card fully cropped OUT (no card pixels present). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed product crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance/exposure move the agent applied per frame.

outputs.name: variant_seal_oxblood.jpg
outputs.spec: Seasonal colorway variant of the Retinol Night hero (capture 6): the coloured wax-seal band on the dropper collar deepened from warm terracotta-red to a rich oxblood/burgundy house colour via a masked, luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl pass pair (a small within-family hue nudge plus a saturation/luminance drop — an in-band adjacent shift, NO near-complementary rotation) riding the band's existing luminosity, so its sheen highlights and cast shadow stay natural and the glass, cap and sweep are untouched — no whole-image overlay, no flat fill.

outputs.name: botanical_panel_green.png
outputs.spec: Brand-green halftone/duotone botanical side-panel texture derived from the supplied leaf line art (crop-to-bounds -> halftone -> single-hue green tint), print-clean as a spot-style panel; binds into every label via the template's shared @panel image frame.

outputs.name: soravell_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the SORAVELL BOTANICS wordmark + sprig mark, traced ONLY after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured paper ground or skew; binds into every label via the shared @wordmark image frame and is reusable on the carton.

outputs.name: carton_packshot.png
outputs.spec: High-resolution mockup packshot: the finished foil-embossed carton sample (mark_ref_02) lifted onto a clean ground via image_remove_background and reframed by downscale — the correct route for a PHOTOGRAPH (it is NOT vectorized). Satisfies the brief's high-res mockup deliverable.

outputs.name: dieline_print.pdf
outputs.spec: Print PDF EXPORTED from the authored carton dieline .ai with cut/fold lines, 3 mm bleed, registration marks and CMYK preserved (connector exports the genuine .ai, it does not author it).

outputs.name: Soravell_Labels_perSKU_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready 70x90mm + 3mm-bleed CMYK label pages — ONE single-record label per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each page binds its product_name/key_actives/volume/batch verbatim from the roster with its matching grey-card-neutralized product crop (via @photo), the vectorized wordmark in the masthead (via @wordmark) and the brand-green botanical panel (via @panel) — all by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI at trim.

connector_workflow.note: Capture 1 = THE TRAP. This bottle's rosehip oil is GENUINELY deep golden-amber and it was shot under near-neutral light, so its in-frame 18% grey card ALREADY reads neutral. Read THAT card by eye and HOLD white balance (only a whisper of correction, if any); do NOT apply the 'warm the cool cast' move the other frames need or 'cool an imagined blue cast' — either strips the amber the brand sells and pushes the card off-neutral. Level frame, no straighten. Report the (near-zero) move applied.

Crop the neutralized frame to the label product frame, framing on the bottle with the grey card cropped OUT (this product crop carries no card). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Name it to the Rosehip Renewal roster row's @photo.
Capture 2 is tilted ~4 deg — level it first (auto_straighten is the only rectify path). Deciding which frames are tilted is part of the work.

Cool bluish fluorescent cast: WARM it (positive temperature) and set tint until the in-frame grey card reads neutral, landing on the shared white point set on frame 1; hold a subtle premium warmth. Report the move.
Crop to the label product frame, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Name to the Niacinamide Clarity row's @photo.

Level frame, warm window light: this must move the OPPOSITE direction from the cool frames — COOL it (negative temperature) until its grey card reads neutral and matches the shared white point. Report the move.
Crop to the label product frame, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Name to the Hyaluronic Hydra row's @photo.
Capture 4 is tilted ~3 deg — level it.

Milder near-trap: cool cast over a GENUINELY golden vitamin-C serum. Warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point, but do NOT desaturate or cool the real gold away chasing an imagined cast — the product colour must survive. Report the move.
Crop to the label product frame, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Name to the Vitamin C Bright row's @photo.

Level frame, flat and underexposed: the dominant move is TONAL — LIFT exposure and add contrast/clarity — then neutralize its grey card to the shared white point without introducing a cast. Report the move.
Crop to the label product frame, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Name to the Squalane Calm row's @photo.
Capture 6 is tilted ~3 deg under warm tungsten — level it. This is the hero for the seasonal seal recolour.

Warm tungsten cast: COOL it (negative temperature) until its grey card reads neutral and matches the shared white point. This neutralized full-res master feeds BOTH its product crop (step 15) AND the masked wax-seal recolour branch (steps 21-24). Report the move.

Crop the neutralized hero to the label product frame (the standard red-seal version that binds into the Retinol Night label), grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Name to the Retinol Night row's @photo.
Capture 7 is tilted ~4 deg, cool cast — level it.
Cool cast over a greenish serum: WARM to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point, but keep the green serum true (do not oversaturate or shift the green). Report the move.
Crop to the label product frame, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Name to the Green Tea Detox row's @photo.

Level frame, overexposed and warm: PULL exposure/highlights down to recover the blown glass, THEN cool to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point — an opposite tonal AND WB move from the underexposed frame 5. Report the move.

Crop to the label product frame, grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Name to the Peptide Firm row's @photo. Captures 1-8 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own grey card.

On the graded hero master, semantically select ONLY the coloured wax-seal band around the dropper collar ('the coloured wax seal band on the dropper cap collar') — isolates the recolour to the part the client wants changed. Selection is semantic, anchored to a named object, never a hue or coordinate region.

Masked recolour pass 1 (consumes hero master + seal mask): keep the band in the red family but deepen it toward oxblood — a small within-band hue nudge (well under 90 deg, an adjacent shift image_adjust_hsl can reliably hold), riding the band's real luminosity so folds/sheen survive. Masked HSL is the ONLY masked recolour path — color_overlay (whole-image) and fill_area (flat dead-fill) are wrong here.

Masked recolour pass 2 (same mask): trim the red-band saturation and settle the luminance so the band lands on the rich oxblood/burgundy house target instead of a bright red — a deepen-and-mute, not a jump to a far hue. Sheen highlights and cast shadow stay intact.

Reframe the finished oxblood-seal variant to the same web/marketing frame as the set. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Standalone seasonal-colorway deliverable (not bound into the standard label).

TRIAGE: mark_ref_01 is flat letter/line art on paper -> route to prep-before-trace. Step 1: the scan sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed — straighten so vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the tilt.
Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the warm off-white paper toward white so the forest-green lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces to mush.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms + sprig only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background to transparency, not a select->invert->fill.
Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the masthead and carton. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded blob.

TRIAGE decoy resolved correctly: mark_ref_02 is a PHOTOGRAPH of foil emboss on textured card, NOT flat art — route it to remove_background to lift the carton sample onto a clean ground. Vectorizing it (like mark_ref_01) would return garbage weave/emboss/highlight paths. This is the wrong-decision failure point that is invisible until the output is opened.
Reframe the knocked-out carton sample to the mockup packshot size by downscale. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. High-res mockup deliverable.
Crop the botanical line art to the label side-panel bounds/aspect. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Convert the line art to a 2-tone halftone dot texture so it prints clean as a spot-style panel (no LPI parameter exists; the tool sets the screen).
Tint the halftone to the brand forest-green as a single-hue spot panel (agent-authored duotone look built from primitives, not a preset). Binds into every label via the shared @panel frame.
EXPORT the client-authored carton dieline .ai to a print PDF (cut/fold/bleed/registration/CMYK preserved). Connector EXPORTS the genuine .ai, it does not author it.

Initialize an upload session for the eight grey-card-neutralized product crops plus the vectorized wordmark SVG and the brand-green botanical panel so the merge can resolve them by the @photo (per-row), @wordmark (shared) and @panel (shared) columns.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @photo/@wordmark/@panel columns resolve to — the per-SKU graded crop, the shared wordmark, and the shared panel.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the eight roster rows (product_name/key_actives/volume/batch) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd, resolving @photo (that row's graded bottle crop), @wordmark (shared vectorized wordmark) and @panel (shared botanical panel) into the template's three merge-wired image frames. [T] needs the user-authored template with real fields + @image columns; produces one label page per SKU.

Export the merged single-record labels to a press-ready ~300 DPI, 3mm-bleed, CMYK PDF, one page per SKU. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document in one call — no per-record named export is attempted; any 'hero' SKU is simply one page of this PDF.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. Eight per-capture grade sub-chains fan out from the raw zip, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization driven to that frame's own in-frame 18% grey card, followed by an image_crop_and_resize to the label product frame (grey card cropped OUT), with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted captures 2/4/6/7 — every neutralization converges on one shared white point (capture 1 held as the trap, capture 4 warmed without killing its gold, capture 5 exposure-lifted, capture 8 exposure-pulled). The Retinol hero's neutralized full-res master (retinol_neutralized, step 14) feeds BOTH its product crop (step 15) AND the recolour branch: image_select_by_prompt(21) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(22) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(23) -> crop_and_resize(24), the two HSL passes both consuming seal_mask. The wordmark runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain on mark_ref_01: straighten(25) -> crisp adjustments(26) -> crop_to_bounds(27) -> remove_background to transparency(28) -> vectorize(29). The triage decoy mark_ref_02 is routed away from the tracer to remove_background(30) -> crop_and_resize(31) = carton packshot. The botanical panel runs crop_and_resize(32) -> halftone(33) -> monochromatic green tint(34). The dieline .ai is exported once by document_render_vector(35). The eight graded crops plus the wordmark SVG and the green panel converge into the upload session(36) -> finalize(37) -> document_merge_data_layout(38), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the roster CSV and emits one label per row, resolving @photo (that row's crop), @wordmark (shared SVG) and @panel (shared texture) into the template's three merge-wired image frames — the only connector-doable path for the wordmark and panel since free-form placement is banned. The merged set is exported once by document_render_layout(39) to the single press-ready ~300 DPI PDF (one page per SKU); no per-record named export is attempted. Nothing after the raw loads originates outside the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 39 connector calls, 15 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grading/masking/halftone/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* export/merge/export), far above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the 2 asset_* upload steps and the auto_straighten auto-ops. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the eight neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision (cool frames warmed, warm frames cooled, one genuinely-golden frame HELD as a trap, one real-gold frame warmed without desaturating, one underexposed frame lifted, one overexposed frame recovered) all forced to converge on one measurable target — the in-frame 18% grey card — so a blanket batch correction cannot pass. Layered on top: a masked luminosity-preserving within-family seal recolour executed as two HSL passes (with a written rationale for why color_overlay and fill_area are both wrong), a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white scan, a same-kind mark TRIAGE (flat art -> trace vs photograph -> remove_background), a crop->halftone->tint agent-authored spot panel, and a three-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no inpainting, no from-scratch layout, no compositing; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used (the label template is a supplied authored .indd with real <<fields>> + @image columns — this removes the original spec's broken merge path); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only reframe pinned to onSubjectClipping='extract'; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature/_highlights/_vibrance_and_saturation/_brightness_and_contrast are all replaced by image_apply_adjustments; document_render_vector and document_render_layout only EXPORT genuine authored files.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION the agent can trip by eye, never a self-measurement): every one of the eight bottle captures carries a physical 18% grey card, and the acceptance test is that each frame's card, graded on its RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master, reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a hair of zero) with all eight matched to one shared white point — a target a naive agent misses, because it must dial DIFFERENT and OPPOSITE-DIRECTION corrections per frame (warm the cool frames 2/4/7, cool the warm frames 3/6/8, lift exposure on the flat frame 5, pull exposure on the overexposed frame 8) and REPORT the per-frame WB/exposure move so 'matched' is verifiable rather than asserted; a blanket batch correction fails. TRAP: capture 1's rosehip serum is GENUINELY golden-amber and was shot under neutral light, so its grey card is already neutral — the naive 'warm the batch / cool an imagined cast' move pushes THAT card off-neutral and strips the real product colour; the correct path reads that card and holds white balance (capture 4 repeats this in a milder form over a real gold). SECOND wrong-decision gate — TRIAGE of two same-kind marks under a neutral scheme (mark_ref_01 / mark_ref_02): one is flat letter art that must be prep-before-traced into a clean SVG, the other is a PHOTOGRAPH of foil emboss on card that must be routed to remove_background for the packshot; vectorizing the photo returns garbage emboss/weave paths, a failure invisible until the SVG is opened. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset neutralization of eight differently-lit shots to one measurable shared white point, each on its own correction axis; (2) a masked, luminosity-preserving within-family recolour (terracotta-red -> oxblood/burgundy wax seal via two image_adjust_hsl passes on a semantic mask, keeping sheen and shadow — the only masked recolour path, not color_overlay or fill_area); (3) prep-before-trace discipline on a skewed off-white margin-padded scan before vectorize; (4) the mark triage. AGENT-AUTHORED look from primitives: the neutralized-to-one-white-point set, the two-pass masked seal recolour, and the crop->halftone->green-tint botanical spot panel are all the agent's craft decisions, not a preset, auto-tone, or supplied .xmp. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (decoupled so no artifact is graded on a region it crops away): (a) grey card neutral (channel spread near zero) and one shared white point, evaluated on all eight RETAINED card-bearing neutralized masters, never on a card-removed product crop; (b) card-EXCLUSION checked separately on the eight product crops that bind into the labels; plus the agent reports per-frame WB/exposure params, the seal recoloured within its mask only, the wordmark a clean skew-free transparent-ground vector, the photographed carton routed to remove_background (not traced), and the merge output page-count = roster row-count = 8 at ~300 DPI. Camera-scale (~4000-4500 px) sources guarantee every ~300 DPI crop is a DOWNSCALE — no upscaling anywhere.
